title: Madhya Pradesh: new places (2026-11-26)
selection: Madhya Pradesh pass: Malwa and Narmada towns (Indore, Mandu, Maheshwar, Omkareshwar), Jabalpur, Chanderi, Burhanpur, Amarkantak, Chitrakoot, Shivpuri and the Panna, Pench and Kuno parks, from MP Tourism destination pages.

MT_JBP.title: Funfair of Jabalpur — Madhya Pradesh Tourism

MT_CHA.title: Beauty of Chanderi — Madhya Pradesh Tourism

MIN1.claim: Indore, Madhya Pradesh's largest city, was shaped by Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar; it has been ranked India's cleanest city and is the home of the Indore gharana of Hindustani music.

evidence.quote: s the largest city in the state of madhya pradesh
Later, Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar , with her keen interest in education and planning, built this city in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
The city is ranked as "the cleanest city in India" for the sixth consecutive year
It is also the birthland of the Indore Gharana of Hindustani Classical Music.

MIN2.claim: Its sights include the seven-storey Rajwada of the Holkars, the all-glass Kanch Mandir Jain temple, the 8 m Bada Ganpati, Lalbagh Palace (1886–1921) and the Annapurna temple.

evidence.quote: The Rajwada's seven-story facade is astounding in its opulence.
The spectacular Kanch Mandir made entirely of glass and mirrors is one of the prime tourist attractions in Indore.
The 8-m-tall Ganesha idol was placed in this modest temple in 1875 by a resident of Ujjain.
Spread over 71.63 acres, the Palace was built between 1886 and 1921

MIN6.claim: Indore was a 16th-century trading hub between the Deccan and Delhi; Rajwada stands near Khajuri Bazar and Lalbagh Palace is in European style.

evidence.quote: A trading hub between the Deccan and Delhi in the 16th century
Rajwada palace, is located near Khajuri Bazar
The architecture of Lal Bagh Palace reflects the European style

MIN3.claim: Indore's signature food is found at Sarafa Bazaar.

evidence.quote: Its signature cuisine, found at sarafa bazaar, is popular across the nation

MIN4.claim: The best time is October to March, at 12–30 °C.

evidence.quote: the best time to visit is between October and March when the weather is conducive enough for sightseeing and outdoor activities.
The temperature during this period ranges between 12 degrees C and 30 degrees C.

MIN5.claim: The airport, 10 km west of the city, has daily flights to Mumbai, Delhi, Bhopal, Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Kolkata and more; buses to Ujjain, Gwalior, Bhopal, Omkareshwar and Maheshwar leave from Sarwate bus station near the railway station.

evidence.quote: The airport in Indore is located 10 kilometres west of the city.
Flights to Mumbai, Delhi, Bhopal, Pune, Nagpur, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Raipur, Jaipur, and Kolkata are available every day.
The Sarwate bus stop is close to the train station
Regular buses to Ujjain, Gwalior, Bhopal, Omkareshwar, and Maheshwar depart from the Sarwate Bus Station

MMD1.claim: Mandu sits at about 2,000 ft on the Vindhyas and is linked to the romance of Baz Bahadur and Rani Roopmati; its 45 km of walls have 12 gateways.

evidence.quote: Mandu is a celebration in stone, of life and joy, and the love of poet-prince Baz Bahadur for his beautiful consort, Rani Roopmati.
Perched along the Vindhya ranges at an altitude of 2,000 feet
The 45 km parapet of walls that encircle Mandu are punctuated by 12 gateways.
combining the charming assertion of the Afghan mode

MMD2.claim: Jahaz Mahal is a 120 m two-storey palace between two lakes; Hoshang Shah's Tomb is India's first marble edifice, studied by Shah Jahan's architects; the Jami Masjid was inspired by the mosque of Damascus.

evidence.quote: This 120-meter-long 'Jahaz Mahal' built between two artificial lakes, Munj Talao and Kapur Talao, is an elegant two-storeyed palace.
It is India's first marble edifice
Shah Jehan sent four of his great architects to study the design and draw inspiration from the tomb.
Inspired by the great mosque of Damascus, the Jami Masjid was conceived on a grand scale

MMD3.claim: Roopmati's Pavilion looks down to the Narmada; Hindola Mahal, the 'swinging palace', has sloping walls.

evidence.quote: From its hilltop perch, this graceful structure with its two pavilions was a retreat of the lovely queen, from where she could see Baz Bahadur's palace and the Narmada flowing through the Nimar plains far below.
it derives the name of 'swinging palace' from its sloping sidewalls.

MMD4.claim: Try dal paniya, and the baobab fruit called Khorasani imli, sold when ripe from February.

evidence.quote: Mandu ka Dal Paniya" is a must-try local delicacy
Locally it is called Khorasani Imli and is used to add tang in dal and curries.
the vendors in Mandu sell the gourd-like fruit, after they have ripened in February.

MMD5.claim: Best July to March (14–30 °C); summers reach 46 °C.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Mandu is between July and March, when the average temperature is comfortable, varying between 14 Degrees Celsius (57 Degrees Fahrenheit) and 30 Degrees Celsius (86 degrees Fahrenheit).
The summers are hot, and the temperature can rise as high as 46 Degrees Celsius

MMD6.claim: Indore airport is 95 km away; Ratlam (130 km) is the nearest railhead; buses from Indore take about 3 hours. MP Tourism runs the Malwa Resort.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Ahilyabai Holkar Airport at Indore (95 km)
The nearest railhead is located at Ratlam, 130 km from Mandu.
From Indore, there are direct buses to Mandu from Gangwal Bus Stand and Sarawate Bus Stand. The journey usually takes around 3 hours.
MPT Malwa Resort, Mandu

MMH1.claim: Maheshwar, on the Narmada, was ancient Mahishmati and the 18th-century capital of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar, who revived the town.

evidence.quote: At the dawn of Indian civilization, it was known as Mahishmati, the capital of King Kartivarjun.
This holy town was revived to its ancient position of importance by the Holkar queen Rani Ahilyabai of Indore.
The town also holds the distinction of being the capital of Rajmata Ahilya Devi Holkar's empire during the 18th century.
finds mentioned in the epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata

MMH2.claim: A weaving centre since the 5th century, Maheshwar makes Maheshwari saris, introduced about 250 years ago by Ahilyabai and revived by the Rehwa Society from 1979.

evidence.quote: A center of handloom weaving since the 5th century, Maheshwar has been producing exquisite Maheshwari sarees and fabric .
Introduced almost 250 years ago by Rani Ahilyabai, these sarees are renowned throughout India for their unique weave.
They started a weaving project involving the local women and called it the Rehwa Society.
Found mostly in cotton, the typical Maheshwari sarees are available with a plain body or stripes and sometimes even with checks

MMH3.claim: Best October to March, though the midday sun is sharp; summers reach 46 °C and winters drop to 5 °C. Pilgrims crowd in at Shivratri and Kartik Purnima, when the three-day Nimar Utsav is held.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Maheshwar is between October and March. However, during the day, even in the winter months, the sun can be very sharp.
The maximum temperature during the summer months can go as high as 46-degree Celsius, while in the winters it can go down to 5-degree Celsius.
Loads of pilgrims can be seen in this place during the festivals of Shivratri and Kartik Purnima.
It is an annual 3-day event held at Maheshwar that comprises music, dance, drama, and activities such as boating and canoeing.

MMH4.claim: Maheshwar is about 100 km by road from Indore and 80 km from Omkareshwar; MP Tourism runs the Narmada Retreat.

evidence.quote: From Indore, it is almost 100 km away by road
From Omkareshwar, it is situated almost 80 km away by road.
Book your stay at the MPT Narmada Retreat

MMH5.claim: Ahilyabai's fort and palace, with her life-size statue on a throne, stands above the Narmada ghat; the Ahilyeshwar temple is her chhatri.

evidence.quote: The Ahilyabai fort and palace house a beautiful life-size statue of Rani Ahilyabai on a throne and a Shiva temple.
It is also known as Ahilyabai's chhatri
Situated at the foot of Ahilyabai fort, this place is a must-visit destination in the holy town of Maheshwar.
Throughout the day a kaleidoscope of rural India can be seen here, in the pilgrims and holy men who sit here in silent meditation.

MOK1.claim: Omkareshwar, about 80 km southeast of Indore, takes its name from an island shaped like 'Om' and has one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

evidence.quote: Nestled about 80 km southeast of the bustling city of Indore, the sacred town of Omkareshwar draws its name from an island shaped like the sacred syllable "OM"
This serene town is home to one of the 12 revered Jyotirlingas, the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga

MOK2.claim: The island temple has a 14 ft assembly hall on 60 pillars and five floors; Mamleshwar on the south bank is held to be the same Jyotirlinga.

evidence.quote: Within the temple complex stands a spacious assembly hall soaring to a height of 14 feet, supported by an array of 60 majestic pillars.
This architectural marvel encompasses a total of five floors
Mamleshwar Jyotirlinga, also known as the Amreshwar temple is situated on the mainland on the south bank of Narmada.
both Mamleshwar and Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga are believed to be manifestations of the same sacred entity.

MOK3.claim: Ekatma Dham honours Adi Shankaracharya; its 108 ft Statue of Oneness was installed in September 2023.

evidence.quote: The 'Statue of Oneness,' a 108-ft tribute to Adi Shankaracharya was installed in September 2023 under this project.
It was within these sacred caverns that Adi Shankaracharya experienced enlightenment under the wise guidance of his Guru, Govinda Bhagvatpada.

MOK4.claim: Other sights: the 11th-century Gauri Somnath and Kedareshwar temples, the 13th-century Siddhanath ruins, the Govinda Bhagavatpada caves, the 270 ft Mamleshwar Setu and the daily Shayan Aarti at Kotitirtha Ghat.

evidence.quote: Believed to be built in the 11th century AD the Gauri Somnath temple was built by the Parmars.
The ruin of this 13th-century marvel is another stunning architectural gem in Omkareshwar.
It is a 270 ft. hanging bridge that enhances the beauty of Omkareshwar.
Every day a Shayan Aarti is performed at the local Kotitirtha Ghat

MOK5.claim: Indore airport is about 87 km away; Khandwa (77 km) and Indore (78 km) are the nearest railway stations; cabs and buses run from Indore and Ujjain.

evidence.quote: The closest airport to Omkareshwar is Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport in Indore, nearly 87 km from the town.
The closest broad-gauge railway stations to the town are Khandwa railway station (77 km) and Indore junction (78 km).
You can travel to the nearest cities of Indore and Ujjain and book a cab or bus ride to the town.

MJB1.claim: Jabalpur lies in a rocky basin about 9.6 km from the Narmada and about 22 km from the Marble Rocks gorge at Bhedaghat; its name is linked to the sage Jabali.

evidence.quote: the meaning of the name "Jabalpur" is said to have been named after the sage Jabali
About 9.6 km from the Narmada river, in a rocky basin surrounded by low hills, is where Jabalpur is located.
It is roughly 22 kilometres from the Narmada Gorge in Bhedaghat, where the river flows between the renowned Marble rock hill.

MJB2.claim: Sights include the 10th-century Chausath Yogini temple, India's largest yogini temple; the Balancing Rock near Madan Mahal fort; and the 23 m Shiva statue at Kachnar City.

evidence.quote: It was constructed by the Kalachuri king Yuvarajadeva I in the 10th century.
It is the largest yogini temple in India, with an exterior circumference of 41m.
The rocks lie very close to the Madan Mahal Fort in Deotal.
The statue is 23 metres (76 feet) tall and sits on top of a cavern housing replicas of Shiva Lingams

MJB3.claim: Jabalpur can be visited all year, but the monsoon (July–September) is best for the waterfalls.

evidence.quote: The city can be toured throughout the year, however, the best time to visit Jabalpur is during the monsoon season.
Between July and September, the water cascading from the hills in and around Jabalpur will mesmerize you with its natural beauty.

MJB4.claim: Dumna Airport, 20 km away, has flights to Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Nagpur, Bhopal and Indore; Jabalpur is a major West Central Railway station and on NH 7. MP Tourism runs the Kalchuri Residency.

evidence.quote: The closest airport, Dumna Airport, is located 20 kilometres away from Jabalpur city.
Through air travel, Jabalpur is well-connected to Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Nagpur, Bhopal, and Indore.
Jabalpur Railway Station is a significant West Central Railway station.
MPT Kalchuri Residency, Jabalpur

MJB5.claim: Dhuandhar falls drop 98 ft; Gandhi's ashes were immersed at Tilwara Ghat; Dumna Nature Park covers 1,500 hectares.

evidence.quote: dive from 98 ft. to create Dhuandhar waterfall
Dunna nature park is one of the biggest nature parks with an area of 1500 hectares
Visit the point where Mahatma Gandhi's ashes were immersed at Tilwara Ghat

MCH1.claim: Chanderi, in Ashoknagar district, is famous for its fabric and its 11th-century monuments — Chanderi Fort, Badal Mahal and the Battisi Baoli; it is about 103 km from Jhansi and 214 km from Bhopal.

evidence.quote: A small town located in the Ashoknagar district of Madhya Pradesh, Chanderi is known for its exquisite fabric.
The history of this magnificent town dates back to the 11th century
Visit iconic monuments like the Chanderi Fort , Badal Mahal and the largest baoli (a stepwell), also known as the Battisti Baoli.
This beautiful destination is located around 103 km from Jhansi and 214 km from Bhopal .

MCH2.claim: Chanderi fabric is woven in almost every house — around 5,000 looms and 9,000 weavers in 2017 — in silk cotton, cotton and silk with gold and silver zari motifs.

evidence.quote: The identity of this quaint town is the beautiful Chanderi fabric, which is woven in almost every house here.
As of 2017, there were around 5,000 looms and more than 9,000 weavers in Chanderi
The fabrics woven here are mostly silk cotton, Chanderi cotton, and pure silk.
Gold and silver zari are then used for embroidering beautiful motifs on the saree

MCH3.claim: The Handloom Park (2017) and Pranpur weaving village, 4 km away, show the craft; the town has a Jama Masjid without minarets and once had 1,200 baolis.

evidence.quote: visit the Handloom Park in Chanderi, believed to be the first handloom park in Asia, launched in 2017.
Pranpur village is a serene haven just 4 kilometres from Chanderi.
The only jama masjid in india without minars is found here
Chanderi is known to have had 1200 baolis in the past

MCH4.claim: Best October to February. Gwalior airport is about 214 km away; Lalitpur (40 km) and Ashok Nagar (50 km) are the nearest stations. MP Tourism runs Kila Kothi and Tana Bana.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Chanderi is between the months of October and February
Take a flight to Gwalior Airport, situated around 214 km far from Chanderi.
The nearest railway stations are the Lalitpur Railway Station (around 40 km away) and Ashok Nagar Railway Station (around 50 km away).
MPT Kila Kothi Price

MCH5.claim: Buses run from Indore, Bhopal and Ujjain; MP Tourism also runs Tana Bana.

evidence.quote: You can also take a bus from nearby cities like Indore , Bhopal and Ujjain .
MPT Tana Bana

MBU1.claim: Burhanpur, founded in 1400 on the Tapti, was the Mughal capital in the Deccan and a gateway to southern India, long under Shah Jahan's patronage.

evidence.quote: Founded in 1400 AD along the serene banks of the Tapti River, Burhanpur is a treasure chest of Mughal heritage waiting to be explored.
Once the flourishing capital of the Mughal Kingdom in the Deccan, this historic city served as the strategic gateway to southern India.
For decades, it remained under the patronage of Emperor Shah Jahan

MBU2.claim: Sights: the ruined Shahi Qila with its painted hammam, the 1589 Jama Masjid, Aahukhana — where Mumtaz Mahal is believed to have been first buried — the 'Black Taj', a Jai Singh observatory and the Badi Sangat gurdwara.

evidence.quote: Though in ruins today, its hammam with Persian art and the famed ceiling painting believed to be commissioned by Shah Jahan make it a must-visit.
An elegant mosque built in 1589, known for its intricate arches and peaceful courtyard.
It is believed to be the place where Mumtaz Mahal was temporarily buried before being taken to Agra.
A serene spiritual stop connected to Guru Nanak Dev ji’s visit during his travels.

MBU3.claim: Best October to March. Try Burhanpuri jalebi, daraba, Mughlai kebabs and korma, and mawa jalebi.

evidence.quote: The ideal time to explore Burhanpur is from October to March.
Burhanpuri jalebi – thick, crispy, and iconic Daraba – a sweet dish made from semolina Mughlai kebabs and korma
Khopra pak and mawa jalebi – must-try sweets

MBU4.claim: Indore airport is about 180 km away; Burhanpur station is on the Mumbai–Delhi line. MP Tourism runs the Tapti Retreat.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Indore (around 180 km), well connected to major cities.
Burhanpur Railway Station lies on the Mumbai–Delhi line, making it easily accessible.
MPT Tapti Retreat, Burhanpur

MBU5.claim: Summers are hot and the monsoon brings greenery and heavy showers; roads link Burhanpur to Indore, Khandwa and Jalgaon. There is also a Jai Singh observatory.

evidence.quote: Summers can be quite hot, while the monsoon season brings lush greenery but occasional heavy showers.
Well-connected by highways to Indore, Khandwa, Jalgaon, and other nearby cities.
A remarkable astronomical site built by Raja Jai Singh

MAK1.claim: Amarkantak, called Teerthraj, is where the Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet in the Maikal hills; the Narmada, Sone and Johila rivers rise here.

evidence.quote: Amarkantak is a well known Hindu pilgrimage destination that is popularly known as "Teerthraj" - "the king of pilgrimages".
It is the meeting point of the Vindhya and the Satpura Ranges, with the Maikal Hills being the prominent one among them.
Three rivers - the holy Narmada, the Sone and the Johila emerge from the womb of Amarkantak.

MAK2.claim: The Narmada Udgam temple marks the river's source; the Narmada falls at Kapil Dhara, and a 1 km trek leads to Dugdh Dhara. The Shri Yantra Mandir and Kabir Chabutra are other sights.

evidence.quote: A rising stream of Narmada can be seen at The Narmada Udgam Temple which is the most visited place in Amarkantak.
The holy Narmada pours downhill as a gigantic waterfall forms the Kapil Dhara waterfall.
People take a one-kilometre trek from the Kapil Dhara to the next Narmada fall which is Dugdh Dhara.
Mystic poet, Sant Kabir, is said to have meditated at Kabirchabutra, Amarkantak

MAK3.claim: Best September to February; Narmada Jayanti, Makar Sankranti and Shiv Chaturdashi are winter festivals.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Amarkantak is between September to February.
Narmada Jayanti, Makar Sankranti and Shiv Chaturdashi are celebrated during winters with great enthusiasm.

MAK4.claim: Jabalpur (228 km) and Raipur (230 km) are the nearest airports; Pendra Road, 42 km, the nearest station; buses run from Rewa, Jabalpur, Bilaspur and Raipur. MP Tourism runs Holiday Homes.

evidence.quote: The nearest airports to Amarkantak are Jabalpur at 228 km and Raipur at 230 km.
The closest railhead to Amarkantak is situated at Pendra Road in Chattisgarh at 42 km.
There is the option of direct buses from Rewa, Allahabad, Mandla, Seoni, Bilaspur, Katni, Jabalpur, and Raipur.
MPT Holiday Homes, Amarkantak

MAK5.claim: Amarkantak has a Kalachuri group of temples and forests rich in medicinal plants.

evidence.quote: The Kalchuri Group of Temples: Architectural Heritage of Amarkantak
The forests surrounding Amarkantak have a rich variety of plants with medicinal properties

MCK1.claim: Chitrakoot lies in the northern Vindhya hills; tradition holds that Ram, Sita and Lakshman spent eleven of their fourteen years of exile here.

evidence.quote: Chitrakoot is a tranquil city situated amidst the serene northern hills of the Vindhya Ranges.
Legend has it that within these verdant forests of Chitrakoot, Lord Ram, Goddess Sita and Lakshman spent eleven of their fourteen years of exile.

MCK2.claim: Raghav Prayag Ghat at the Mandakini–Pataru confluence glows with diyas and boats at dusk; Janaki Kund is 2 km from Ram Ghat; Hanuman Dhara is a hilltop temple with city views.

evidence.quote: Raghav Prayag Ghat lies at the sacred confluence of the Mandakini and Pataru rivers and is a vibrant hub of cultural activity.
As the day unwinds, the ghat transforms into a kaleidoscope of sound and colour, lit with diyas and the colourfully decorated boats
Located 2 km from the renowned Ram Ghat, the serene Janaki Kund is an ancient and religious location.
One can get a spectacular bird eye view of the city, by climbing atop this hill temple.

MCK3.claim: Pilgrims walk the 5 km parikrama around Kamadgiri, lined with temples; the Gupt Godavari caves are 18 km from town.

evidence.quote: Devotees circumambulate the 5 km long path here, known as the Parikrama Marg; a lot of significant temples lie on this path.
There is a pair of caves here, located 18 km from the city centre.

MCK4.claim: MP Tourism runs the Tourist Bungalow and Mandakini Resort.

evidence.quote: MPT Tourist Bungalow, Chitrakoot
MPT Mandakini Resort, Chitrakoot

MCK5.claim: Sages, saints and poets have long come to Chitrakoot; Sita is said to have bathed at Janaki Kund.

evidence.quote: Over the ages, Chitrakoot has been a sanctuary for revered sages, saints, poets, and visionaries
who is believed to have taken a bath here, during her exile period with Lord Ram.

MSV1.claim: Shivpuri, about 120 km south of Gwalior, is known for its forests and the Scindias' royal chhatris; it passed to the Scindias in 1804 and was a royal hunting ground.

evidence.quote: Located approximately 120 km south of Gwalior, the city is blessed with diverse flora and fauna, as well as marvellous architectural complexes.
served as the ancestral homeland of the Kachhawaha Rajputs until 1804 when it came under the rule of the Scindias.
Shivpuri's lush forest cover made it a favourite hunting spot for royal families and Mughal emperors.
the intricately embellished Royal Chhatris, George Castle, and the nearby Narwar Fort

MSV2.claim: Madhav National Park (355 sq km) has tigers, sambar, chinkara, blackbuck and sloth bear and is MP's 9th tiger reserve; Sakhya Sagar has a boat club, winter birds and mugger crocodiles. George Castle stands inside the park.

evidence.quote: Covering a rich forest area of 355 sq km, the park is home to distinct wildlife such as Tigers, Sambar, Chausingha, Blackbuck, Sloth Bear, Chinkara, the Indian Gazelle, and the Chital.
as the 9th tiger reserve of the state
Along the lake's shore is a boat club, providing visitors with a captivating view of migratory birds, especially during winter
The stunning George Castle is situated deep within the untamed forests of Madhav National Park.

MSV3.claim: Winter is the best season; summers reach 40 °C.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit this location is during winter because it offers comfortable travel conditions and cooler temperatures compared to other seasons.
Summers generally bring temperatures as high as 40 degrees Celsius

MSV4.claim: Gwalior airport is 130 km away; Jhansi (97 km) and Gwalior (120 km) are the nearest stations. Kuno National Park is 60 km away. MP Tourism runs the Tourist Village.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport to Shivpuri is the Gwalior airport, located at a distance of 130 km from the city centre.
The nearest railway stations are Jhansi Junction (97 km) and Gwalior Junction (120 km).
Kuno National Park, located 60 km from Shivpuri
MPT Tourist Village, Shivpuri

MPN1.claim: Panna National Park, in the Vindhya hills 27 km from Khajuraho, is a dry deciduous tiger reserve of plateaus and gorges along the Ken river.

evidence.quote: a haven for wildlife enthusiasts nestled in the Vindhya Hills of northern Madhya Pradesh.
This crucial tiger habitat boasts a dynamic dry deciduous forest, adorned with extensive plateaus and gorges
just 27 km from Khajuraho
The Ken River, gracefully winding through the reserve

MPN2.claim: Besides tigers there are leopards, wild dogs, wolves, hyenas and sloth bears, and over 200 bird species; seven of India's nine vulture species occur here, and gharials can be seen at the Ken Gharial sanctuary.

evidence.quote: Panna National Park is also home to Leopards, Wild Dogs, Wolves, Hyenas, and smaller Cats.
For bird enthusiasts, Panna offers a symphony of avian delights with over 200 species, including migratory birds.
Out of the nine vulture species found in India, seven species are found in Panna.
can be spotted at Ken Ghariyal sanctuary

MPN3.claim: MP Tourism recommends October to June. Khajuraho airport is 25 km away and Khajuraho station 22 km; Satna Junction is 88 km.

evidence.quote: Plan your visit between October and June to make the most of your Panna National Park experience.
The nearest airport is Khajuraho Airport, situated 25 km away.
The nearest railway stations are Khajuraho railway station (22 km away) and Satna Railway Junction (88 km away).

MPN4.claim: MP Tourism lists safari prices of ₹2,450 on weekdays and ₹3,050 on weekends and government holidays; gypsy and guide charges vary. It runs the Madla Jungle Camp.

evidence.quote: Panna National Park Ticket Price Weekdays: Rs 2,450 Weekends and Government Holidays: Rs 3,050
Please note that Gypsy and Local Guide prices may vary
Madla Jungle Camp in Panna

MPN5.claim: Sambar, chital and chowsingha live in the woods; nilgai and chinkara on the grasslands.

evidence.quote: The wooded areas are dotted with Sambar and you may catch glimpses of Chital and Chowsingha.
Blue Bulls and Chinkara gracefully roam the open grasslands

MPC1.claim: Pench, 93 km from Nagpur and 201 km from Jabalpur, is named after the Pench river and inspired Kipling's The Jungle Book; it has been a tiger reserve since 1992.

evidence.quote: 201 km from Jabalpur and 93 km from Nagpur, Pench is famous for its Tiger Reserve
It is named after the Pench river that flows through it.
Pench National Park inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'
Art of project tiger since 1992

MPC2.claim: Its teak and mixed deciduous forest holds chital, leopard, sambar, gaur, chowsingha and chinkara, and over 285 bird species.

evidence.quote: it is a bit moist teak forest and dry mixed deciduous forest.
it also shelters a dense population of cheetal (Spotted Deer), followed by leopard, sambhar, gaur (Indian bison), chousingha (four-horned antelope), chinkara (Indian gazelle)
Home to over 285 resident and migratory birds

MPC3.claim: Best October to February; November to March for birds. Safaris are closed in the monsoon and are booked at forest.mponline.gov.in.

evidence.quote: October to February can be considered the best time to visit Pench when the weather is pleasant and the jungle looks lush.
November to March could be the best months for bird watching
You should avoid Monsoon season if you are looking forward to jungle safari as it is kept closed
You can book your slot for safari by visiting https://forest.mponline.gov.in

MPC4.claim: Nagpur airport and station are about 130 km away; Jabalpur is about 210 km. MP Tourism runs Kiplings Court.

evidence.quote: the Nagpur Airport is situated at a distance of about 130 km
Nagpur railway station is the closest railhead from Pench with good connectivity, and it is situated approximately 130 kilometres away.
MPT Kiplings Court, Pench

MPC5.claim: The Jungle Book places are at Alikatta village and the Seeonee hills.

evidence.quote: The places described in 'The Jungle Book' are the locations marked at Alikatta village and the Seeonee hills.

MKU1.claim: Kuno National Park, in Sheopur and Shivpuri districts, covers 74,200 hectares and is the only national park in India with cheetahs, reintroduced under Project Cheetah from 17 September 2022.

evidence.quote: Kuno National Park, also known as Kuno Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary, is situated in the Sheopur and Shivpuri districts of the state, covering an expansive land area of 74,200 hectares.
Kuno National Park stands out as the only national park in India that is home to Cheetahs.
Cheetahs were reintroduced in India after more than 70 years as part of Project Cheetah on September 17, 2022.
Eight cheetahs were translocated from Namibia

places.name: Indore
places.summary: Madhya Pradesh's biggest city — Holkar palaces, a glass temple and the Sarafa night food market.
places.seoTitle: Indore: Rajwada, Kanch Mandir, Sarafa Food and Getting There
places.seoDescription: Indore, MP's largest city: the Holkars' Rajwada and Lalbagh Palace, the glass Kanch Mandir, Sarafa Bazaar food, flights and buses, best October–March.

overview.text: Indore is the largest city in Madhya Pradesh, a 16th-century trading hub between the Deccan and Delhi that Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar later shaped with her interest in planning and learning. It has been ranked India's cleanest city several years running and is the birthplace of the Indore gharana of Hindustani classical music. The Holkars left their mark in the seven-storey Rajwada near Khajuri Bazar and in the European-style Lalbagh Palace, built between 1886 and 1921. Other sights include the Kanch Mandir, a Jain temple made entirely of glass and mirrors, and the 8 m Bada Ganpati. Above all, Indore is a food city: its signature street food is served at Sarafa Bazaar. It is also the usual gateway to Ujjain, Omkareshwar, Maheshwar and Mandu.

best_time.text: October to March, when temperatures range from 12 to 30 °C.

how_to_reach.text: Indore airport, 10 km west of the city, has daily flights to Mumbai, Delhi, Bhopal, Pune, Nagpur, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Raipur, Jaipur and Kolkata. Regular buses to Ujjain, Gwalior, Bhopal, Omkareshwar and Maheshwar leave from Sarwate bus station, near the railway station.

places.name: Mandu
places.summary: A ruined Afghan fortress-city on the Vindhyas — Jahaz Mahal, Hoshang Shah's marble tomb and Roopmati's pavilion.
places.seoTitle: Mandu: Jahaz Mahal, Roopmati's Pavilion and How to Get There
places.seoDescription: Mandu on the Vindhyas: Jahaz Mahal, Hoshang Shah's Tomb, Jami Masjid and Roopmati's Pavilion; dal paniya, best July–March, 95 km from Indore.

overview.text: Mandu is a ruined fortress-city on the Vindhya range at about 2,000 ft, ringed by 45 km of walls pierced by 12 gateways. It is remembered for the love of the poet-prince Baz Bahadur and Rani Roopmati, whose hilltop pavilion looks down to the Narmada on the Nimar plain. Its Afghan-style buildings include the 120 m Jahaz Mahal, a two-storey 'ship palace' between two lakes; Hoshang Shah's Tomb, India's first marble building, which Shah Jahan's architects came to study; the Jami Masjid, modelled on the great mosque of Damascus; and the Hindola Mahal with its sloping 'swinging' walls. Local food includes dal paniya and the tangy fruit of Mandu's baobab trees.

best_time.text: July to March, with temperatures of about 14–30 °C. Summers are hot, up to 46 °C.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest airport is Indore, 95 km away. Ratlam, 130 km, is the nearest railhead, though most visitors come via Indore. Direct buses from Indore's Gangwal and Sarwate bus stands take about 3 hours.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs the Malwa Resort in Mandu.

places.name: Maheshwar
places.summary: Ahilyabai Holkar's temple town on the Narmada — fort, ghats and handwoven Maheshwari saris.
places.seoTitle: Maheshwar: Ahilya Fort, Narmada Ghats and Maheshwari Saris
places.seoDescription: Maheshwar on the Narmada: Ahilyabai Holkar's fort and ghats, Maheshwari saris from the Rehwa Society, Nimar Utsav, 100 km from Indore; best October–March.

overview.text: Maheshwar sits on the bank of the Narmada and is ancient Mahishmati, mentioned in the epics. In the 18th century it became the capital of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar, the pious Holkar queen who revived the town. Her fort and palace rise above the river, with a life-size statue of the queen on her throne, and below it the Narmada ghat is busy all day with pilgrims and holy men; nearby is the Ahilyeshwar temple, her chhatri. Maheshwar has been a weaving centre since the 5th century, and its Maheshwari saris — introduced about 250 years ago by Ahilyabai — were revived from 1979 by the Rehwa Society. Pilgrims crowd in at Shivratri and Kartik Purnima.

best_time.text: October to March, though the midday sun is sharp even in winter. Summers reach 46 °C and winter nights drop to 5 °C. The three-day Nimar Utsav around Kartik Purnima brings music, dance and boating.

how_to_reach.text: Maheshwar is about 100 km by road from Indore and 80 km from Omkareshwar.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs the Narmada Retreat.

places.name: Omkareshwar
places.summary: A Jyotirlinga on an Om-shaped island in the Narmada, with Adi Shankaracharya's 108 ft Statue of Oneness.
places.seoTitle: Omkareshwar: Jyotirlinga Island, Ekatma Dham, How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Omkareshwar, 80 km from Indore: the Jyotirlinga on an Om-shaped Narmada island, Mamleshwar, the 108 ft Statue of Oneness, ghats, bridges and getting there.

overview.text: Omkareshwar lies about 80 km southeast of Indore, where an island in the Narmada is shaped like the sacred syllable Om. On it stands the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, one of the twelve, with an assembly hall raised on 60 pillars within a five-storey temple; across the river on the south bank, Mamleshwar is believed to be a manifestation of the same Jyotirlinga. The town also has the 11th-century Gauri Somnath temple, the ruins of the 13th-century Siddhanath temple and the Govinda Bhagavatpada caves, where Adi Shankaracharya is said to have found enlightenment. That link is honoured at Ekatma Dham, whose 108 ft Statue of Oneness was installed in 2023. A 270 ft hanging bridge crosses the river, and a Shayan Aarti is held each evening at Kotitirtha Ghat.

how_to_reach.text: Indore airport is about 87 km away. The nearest railway stations are Khandwa (77 km) and Indore (78 km). Cabs and buses run from Indore and Ujjain.

places.name: Jabalpur
places.summary: The gateway to Bhedaghat's Marble Rocks — Chausath Yogini, the Balancing Rock and Madan Mahal fort.
places.seoTitle: Jabalpur: Marble Rocks, Chausath Yogini and Getting There
places.seoDescription: Jabalpur, 22 km from Bhedaghat's Marble Rocks: Chausath Yogini temple, Balancing Rock, Madan Mahal, Kachnar City Shiva; flights, trains and the best season.

overview.text: Jabalpur lies in a rocky basin ringed by low hills, about 9.6 km from the Narmada; tradition links its name to the sage Jabali, who meditated on the river's banks. It is the base for the Narmada's most famous stretch, the Marble Rocks gorge at Bhedaghat about 22 km away, where the Dhuandhar falls drop 98 ft. The 10th-century Chausath Yogini temple, built by the Kalachuri king Yuvarajadeva I, is the largest yogini temple in India. In the city itself are the hilltop Madan Mahal fort, the Balancing Rock beside it, the 23 m Shiva statue at Kachnar City and Tilwara Ghat, where Mahatma Gandhi's ashes were immersed. The monsoon is the best season for the waterfalls.

best_time.text: Jabalpur can be visited all year; July to September is best for the waterfalls around the city.

how_to_reach.text: Dumna Airport, 20 km from the city, has flights to Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Nagpur, Bhopal and Indore. Jabalpur is a major West Central Railway station with trains from many cities, and it sits on NH 7.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs the Kalchuri Residency.

places.name: Chanderi
places.summary: A weaving town with 11th-century roots — Chanderi Fort, Badal Mahal, stepwells and its famous saris.
places.seoTitle: Chanderi: Fort, Stepwells and Chanderi Saris
places.seoDescription: Chanderi, 103 km from Jhansi: Chanderi Fort, Badal Mahal and Battisi Baoli, the Handloom Park and Pranpur weavers' village; best October–February.

overview.text: Chanderi is a small town in Ashoknagar district, about 103 km from Jhansi, known across India for its fabric. Weaving goes on in almost every house — around 5,000 looms and over 9,000 weavers by 2017 — producing saris in silk cotton, cotton and silk, embroidered with gold and silver zari motifs. The town's history goes back to the 11th century, and its monuments include the hilltop Chanderi Fort, Badal Mahal and the great Battisi Baoli stepwell; Chanderi once had around 1,200 baolis, and its Jama Masjid is said to be the only one in India without minarets. To see weaving up close, visit the Handloom Park or the weavers' village of Pranpur, 4 km away.

best_time.text: October to February, when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest railway stations are Lalitpur (about 40 km) and Ashok Nagar (about 50 km). Gwalior airport is about 214 km away. Buses run from Indore, Bhopal and Ujjain.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs two stays in Chanderi: Kila Kothi and Tana Bana.

places.name: Burhanpur
places.summary: The Mughals' Deccan capital on the Tapti — Shahi Qila's hammam, the Jama Masjid and Mumtaz Mahal's first resting place.
places.seoTitle: Burhanpur: Mughal Heritage on the Tapti, Food and Getting There
places.seoDescription: Burhanpur on the Tapti: Shahi Qila and its hammam, the 1589 Jama Masjid, Aahukhana and the Black Taj; jalebi and daraba; on the Mumbai–Delhi rail line.

overview.text: Burhanpur was founded in 1400 on the banks of the Tapti and became the Mughals' capital in the Deccan, the strategic gateway to southern India; for decades it enjoyed the patronage of Shah Jahan. The city is full of that history. The Shahi Qila palace on the river is in ruins, but its hammam keeps Persian-style art and a famous ceiling painting believed to have been commissioned by Shah Jahan. The Jama Masjid of 1589 has graceful arches around a quiet courtyard, and at Aahukhana, a royal retreat, Mumtaz Mahal is believed to have been buried before her body was taken to Agra. There is also a Jai Singh observatory and the Badi Sangat gurdwara, linked to Guru Nanak's travels.

best_time.text: October to March, when the weather suits heritage walks. Summers are hot, and the monsoon brings greenery and heavy showers.

how_to_reach.text: Burhanpur station is on the Mumbai–Delhi rail line. The nearest airport is Indore, about 180 km away. Roads link it to Indore, Khandwa and Jalgaon.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs the Tapti Retreat.

places.name: Amarkantak
places.summary: The source of the Narmada in the Maikal hills — Narmada Udgam, Kapil Dhara falls and Kalachuri-era temples.
places.seoTitle: Amarkantak: Source of the Narmada, Waterfalls and Temples
places.seoDescription: Amarkantak, where the Narmada rises: Narmada Udgam temple, Kapil Dhara and Dugdh Dhara falls, Kalachuri temples; best September–February; Pendra Road 42 km.

overview.text: Amarkantak, known as Teerthraj, the king of pilgrimages, sits where the Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet in the Maikal hills. Three rivers rise here — the Narmada, the Sone and the Johila — and the Narmada Udgam temple, built around the Narmada's source, is the town's most visited shrine. The Narmada then pours over the Kapil Dhara falls, and a 1 km walk leads on to the Dugdh Dhara falls. Other sights include the Shri Yantra Mandir, the Kabir Chabutra where the poet Kabir is said to have meditated, and a group of old temples of the Kalachuri era. The surrounding forests are rich in medicinal plants.

best_time.text: September to February. Narmada Jayanti, Makar Sankranti and Shiv Chaturdashi fall in winter.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest station is Pendra Road in Chhattisgarh, 42 km away. The nearest airports are Jabalpur (228 km) and Raipur (230 km). Direct buses run from Rewa, Jabalpur, Bilaspur, Raipur and other towns.

places.name: Chitrakoot
places.summary: Ram's forest of exile in the Vindhya hills — evening ghats on the Mandakini and the Kamadgiri parikrama.
places.seoTitle: Chitrakoot: Ram Ghat, Kamadgiri Parikrama and Where to Stay
places.seoDescription: Chitrakoot in the Vindhya hills, linked to Ram's exile: Raghav Prayag and Ram Ghat, Janaki Kund, Hanuman Dhara, the 5 km Kamadgiri parikrama, Gupt Godavari.

overview.text: Chitrakoot is a quiet pilgrim town in the northern hills of the Vindhya range, surrounded by forest and rivers. Tradition holds that Ram, Sita and Lakshman spent eleven of their fourteen years of exile in these woods, and sages, poets and saints have come here ever since. Life centres on the ghats of the Mandakini: Raghav Prayag Ghat, at its confluence with the Pataru, glows at dusk with diyas and decorated boats. Janaki Kund, where Sita is said to have bathed, is 2 km from Ram Ghat; Hanuman Dhara is a hilltop temple with views over the town; and pilgrims walk the 5 km parikrama around Kamadgiri, lined with temples. The Gupt Godavari caves lie 18 km out.

where_to_stay.text: MP Tourism runs the Tourist Bungalow and the Mandakini Resort.

places.name: Shivpuri
places.summary: The Scindias' forest retreat — marble royal chhatris, Madhav tiger reserve and George Castle.
places.seoTitle: Shivpuri: Royal Chhatris, Madhav National Park, Getting There
places.seoDescription: Shivpuri, 120 km south of Gwalior: the Scindias' royal chhatris, Madhav National Park and George Castle, Sakhya Sagar boating, and Kuno 60 km away.

overview.text: Shivpuri, about 120 km south of Gwalior, was a favourite hunting ground of royal families and Mughal emperors for its thick forests, and it passed from the Kachhawaha Rajputs to the Scindias in 1804. Its best-known monuments are the Scindias' intricately carved Royal Chhatris. Next to the town, Madhav National Park covers 355 sq km of lakes, forest and grassland with tigers, sambar, chinkara, blackbuck and sloth bear; it has become Madhya Pradesh's ninth tiger reserve. George Castle stands deep inside the park, and Sakhya Sagar lake has a boat club, winter birds and mugger crocodiles. Kuno National Park, home of India's reintroduced cheetahs, is 60 km away.

best_time.text: Winter, for cooler and more comfortable conditions. Summers reach 40 °C.

how_to_reach.text: Gwalior airport is 130 km away. The nearest railway stations are Jhansi (97 km) and Gwalior (120 km).

places.summary: A gorge-cut tiger reserve on the Ken river, 27 km from Khajuraho — tigers, vultures and gharials.
places.seoTitle: Panna National Park: Tigers, Ken River, Safari Prices, Season
places.seoDescription: Panna National Park, 27 km from Khajuraho: tigers, leopards, seven vulture species and Ken gharials; open October–June; safari ₹2,450 weekdays (MP Tourism).

overview.text: Panna National Park lies in the Vindhya hills of northern Madhya Pradesh, just 27 km from Khajuraho. It is a tiger reserve of dry deciduous forest, broad plateaus and deep gorges, with the Ken river winding through it. Besides tigers, the park holds leopards, wild dogs, wolves, hyenas and sloth bears, while sambar, chital and chowsingha live in the woods and nilgai and chinkara on the open grassland. Birdlife is rich, with over 200 species, and seven of India's nine vulture species are found here. Gharials can be seen at the Ken Gharial sanctuary. MP Tourism recommends visiting between October and June, and Khajuraho, with its airport and station, makes the easiest base.

places.summary: The Jungle Book forest on the Pench river — tigers, leopards, gaur and dholes, 93 km from Nagpur.
places.seoTitle: Pench National Park: Jungle Book Country, Season and Safaris
places.seoDescription: Pench Tiger Reserve, 93 km from Nagpur: the forest behind Kipling's The Jungle Book, tigers, leopards and 285 bird species; best October–February.

overview.text: Pench National Park takes its name from the Pench river that runs through it and lies 93 km from Nagpur and 201 km from Jabalpur. Its forests are said to have inspired Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book — the Seeonee hills of Mowgli's story are here — and it has been a Project Tiger reserve since 1992. The vegetation is teak and dry mixed deciduous forest, home to tigers and a dense population of chital, along with leopard, sambar, gaur, chowsingha and chinkara. More than 285 resident and migratory bird species have been recorded. Safaris close in the monsoon; October to February is the best season, and November to March is best for birds.

best_time.text: October to February, when the weather is pleasant; November to March for birdwatching. Safaris close in the monsoon.

places.name: Kuno National Park
places.summary: India's cheetah park — grasslands and kardhai forest on the Kuno river, reintroduced cheetahs since 2022.
places.seoTitle: Kuno National Park: Cheetahs, Season and How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Kuno National Park in Sheopur: India's only park with cheetahs (reintroduced 2022), wide grasslands and kardhai forest; closed in the monsoon; best October–March.

overview.text: Kuno National Park, also called Kuno Palpur, spreads over 74,200 hectares of the Sheopur and Shivpuri districts and takes its name from the Kuno river. Its forests are dominated by kardhai, salai and khair, and the kardhai trees famously turn green at the first hint of humidity, before the rains arrive; some of its grasslands are larger than those of Kanha or Bandhavgarh. Kuno is the only national park in India with cheetahs. Under Project Cheetah, eight animals from Namibia were released here on 17 September 2022, the first cheetahs in India in more than 70 years, and more have followed. The park is open all year except in the monsoon, and October to March is the most pleasant time to visit.

best_time.text: October to March. The park is closed to tourism in the monsoon.
